# Self-Hosting & Operations

Reference file for [citations.md](../citations.md).

## Deployment Architecture

Windmill requires three components [4]:

| Component | Role | Port |
|-----------|------|------|
| PostgreSQL | State, job queue, secrets | 5432 |
| Server (windmill_server) | Frontend, API, webhooks | 8000 |
| Workers (windmill_worker) | Job execution | — |

Optional components:
- Windmill LSP (port 3001) — editor intellisense
- Multiplayer service (port 3002) — EE only
- Caddy reverse proxy (ports 80/443) — included in docker-compose

## Docker Compose Setup

Official docker-compose.yml available in the GitHub repository [2][4].
Quick start:

```bash
docker compose up -d
```

Access at http://localhost. Default credentials: `admin@windmill.dev` /
`changeme` [4].

Three files needed: `docker-compose.yml`, `Caddyfile`, `.env` [4].

### Key Environment Variables

| Variable | Purpose | Source |
|----------|---------|--------|
| `DATABASE_URL` | PostgreSQL connection string | [4] |
| `MODE` | "server" or "worker" | [4] |
| `WORKER_GROUP` | Worker group assignment | [4] |
| `NATIVE_MODE=true` | Lightweight native workers | [4] |
| `ENABLE_UNSHARE_PID=true` | PID namespace isolation (default) | [4] |
| `DISABLE_NSJAIL=false` | Filesystem/resource isolation | [4] |

## Resource Requirements

| Configuration | CPU | RAM | Source |
|---------------|-----|-----|--------|
| Standard worker | 1 vCPU | 2 GB | [4] |
| Small worker | — | 1 GB | [4] |
| Large worker | — | >2 GB | [4] |
| Native worker | 0.1 CPU | 128 MB | [4] |
| Rule of thumb | 1 vCPU per worker | 1-2 GB per worker | [4] |

PostgreSQL requires 1 GB shared memory (shm_size) [4].

### Minimal Single-Host Setup

For personal use with a few workflows:
- 1 server + 1-2 standard workers + PostgreSQL
- Estimated minimum: ~2-4 GB RAM total
- Community reports running on Oracle free tier (1 GB) but not recommended [34]

Third-party estimates put hosting costs at $15-20/month for a comfortable
setup vs $5-10/month for n8n [34].

## Podman Compatibility

Not explicitly documented by Windmill [4]. Windmill requires a Docker socket
for container-based script execution (the `# docker` annotation in Bash
scripts) [5][33]. Podman can expose a Docker-compatible socket via
`podman system service`, but this is untested by Windmill's team.

For core Windmill services (server + workers + PostgreSQL), Podman's
Docker Compose compatibility (`podman-compose` or `podman compose`) should
work, as the docker-compose.yml uses standard Docker Compose syntax [4].

## Security Features

| Feature | Details | Source |
|---------|---------|--------|
| PID isolation | Prevents process memory access (Linux) | [4] |
| NSJAIL sandboxing | Filesystem isolation | [4] |
| Workspace encryption | Symmetric key per workspace | [7] |
| Secret masking | First 3 chars visible, rest asterisked in logs | [6] |
| Audit logging | variables.decrypt_secret events (EE) | [6][23] |
| SOC 2 Type II | Compliant | [7] |

## Health Monitoring

Two endpoints [4]:
- `/api/health` (unauthenticated, 5-second cache) — overall status,
  database reachability, worker count
- Detailed health (authenticated) — latency, connection pools, queue depth

OpenTelemetry integration available for external observability [29].

## Execution History & Debugging

### Job Retention

| Plan | Retention | Source |
|------|-----------|--------|
| Community self-hosted | 30 days max | [13] |
| Enterprise self-hosted | Unlimited | [13] |
| Community/Team cloud | 60 days | [13] |
| Enterprise cloud | Unlimited | [13] |

Custom retention configurable in instance settings [13].

### Audit Log Retention

| Plan | Retention | Source |
|------|-----------|--------|
| Community | Redacted | [23] |
| Team cloud | 7 days | [23] |
| Enterprise cloud | 60 days (extendable to 1 year) | [23] |

### Service Log Retention

2-week default, configurable, stored on disk or S3. Three-tier architecture:
in-memory → PostgreSQL → S3 [22].

### Debugging Features

| Feature | Details | Source |
|---------|---------|--------|
| Per-step drill-down | Inputs, outputs, logs, duration, status per node | [26] |
| Visual DAG preview | Graphical flow execution visualization | [26] |
| "Test up to X" | Test partial flows up to a specific step | [26] |
| Restart from failure | Re-run from failed step without replay | [26] |
| Local CLI testing | `deno run -A --watch` or `bun run --watch` | [27] |
| VS Code extension | IDE integration with workspace sync | [28] |
| Full-text search | Enterprise Edition only | [16] |

### Job Progress API

SSE endpoint for real-time monitoring [13]:
`api/job/get/w/{workspace}/jobs_u/getupdate_sse/{id}`

Returns: running status, completion state, new logs, result stream, memory
peak, progress percentage (0-100). Maximum update frequency: 100ms [13].

## Update Process

```bash
docker compose stop windmill_worker
docker compose pull windmill_server
docker compose up -d
```

Database migrations handled automatically. Workers exit cleanly with
30-second timeout [4].

## Volumes & Persistence

| Volume | Mount Point | Purpose |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| db_data | — | PostgreSQL state |
| worker_dependency_cache | /tmp/windmill/cache | Cached dependencies |
| lsp_cache | /root/.cache | LSP cache |
| Docker socket | /var/run/docker.sock | Container execution |

Source: [4]

## Gaps and Limitations

- Exact idle RAM consumption (server + 1 worker + PostgreSQL) not measured
  in documentation
- Podman compatibility untested/undocumented by Windmill
- PostgreSQL version requirements not specified in self-hosting docs
- No published performance benchmarks (jobs/second, latency percentiles)
- Worker autoscaling requires Enterprise Edition [16]
